utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: Abbey’s Taxis. Good morning. Can I help you?

utterances.speaker: Ahmed
utterances.text: Yes, I’d like a taxi please, to go to the airport.

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: OK, no problem. Is the taxi for now?

utterances.speaker: Ahmed
utterances.text: No – can I have the taxi at ten o’clock, please?

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: Ten am. Sure. Just to check – what time is your plane?

utterances.speaker: Ahmed
utterances.text: Oh, it’s at two o’clock.

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: Fine, so there’s lots of time. OK. And what’s your address, please?

utterances.speaker: Ahmed
utterances.text: It’s Lime Street – number 12.

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: Sorry? Lime Street? Lime – L-I-M-E?

utterances.speaker: Ahmed
utterances.text: Yes, that’s right.

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: OK. Twelve Lime Street. Good – and your name, please?

utterances.speaker: Ahmed
utterances.text: It’s Kaynarca, Ahmed.

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: Can you spell your surname, please?

utterances.speaker: Ahmed
utterances.text: K-A-Y-N-A-R-C-A, Kaynarca.

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: K-A-Y-N-A-R-C-A. OK, that’s great. So – a taxi to the airport, 10 o’clock, from 12 Lime Street.

utterances.speaker: Ahmed
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: Oh, sorry – how many people, please? I mean, how many passengers are going to the airport?

utterances.speaker: Ahmed
utterances.text: Oh, just me – only one passenger and one suitcase.

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: OK, that’s fine then. Thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: Ahmed
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Fernando
utterances.text: Hello?

utterances.speaker: Alejandra
utterances.text: Hi. Can I speak to Fernando, please?

utterances.speaker: Fernando
utterances.text: Speaking. Who’s that?

utterances.speaker: Alejandra
utterances.text: Hi, Fernando. It’s Alejandra. I’m a friend of Anna’s. We met last Friday, remember?

utterances.speaker: Fernando
utterances.text: Oh, yes, sure. How are things with you?

utterances.speaker: Alejandra
utterances.text: Great, thanks. And you?

utterances.speaker: Fernando
utterances.text: Yeah, not bad.

utterances.speaker: Alejandra
utterances.text: Fernando, I’m phoning because we’re having a party next Saturday. And perhaps you’d like to come?

utterances.speaker: Fernando
utterances.text: Sure, great. Next Saturday – 14th of July, right?

utterances.speaker: Alejandra
utterances.text: Yes. It starts at 7 o’clock.

utterances.speaker: Fernando
utterances.text: Cool. Can you give me the address?

utterances.speaker: Alejandra
utterances.text: Sure. It’s 134 Markham Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Fernando
utterances.text: Markham. That’s M-A-R-K-A-M, right?

utterances.speaker: Alejandra
utterances.text: Well, no, actually it’s M-A-R-K-H-A-M.

utterances.speaker: Fernando
utterances.text: Oh, sure, of course. OK, Alejandra, so … see you on Friday.

utterances.speaker: Alejandra
utterances.text: Saturday.

utterances.speaker: Fernando
utterances.text: Oh, yeah, duh! Let me just check your phone number – last call on my mobile, here it is: 0789 224 214?

utterances.speaker: Alejandra
utterances.text: That’s it. See you, Juan.

utterances.speaker: Fernando
utterances.text: Um – Fernando.

utterances.speaker: Alejandra
utterances.text: Oops. Sorry! Bye.

1	 Mohamed Salah’s birthday is the 15th of June. 2	 Emma Watson’s birthday is the 15th of April. 3	 Oprah Winfrey’s birthday is the 29th of January. 4	 Adele’s birthday is the 5th of May. 5	 Daniel Kaluuya’s birthday is the 24th of February. 6	 Ed Sheeran’s birthday is the 17th of February.

I’m very busy from Monday to Friday. I always get up at ten to eight, that’s when my alarm clock rings. Then I go downstairs and have breakfast at eight o’clock. Then it’s school time. I leave the house to go to school at half past eight. There’s a break at twenty past ten – I eat an apple. At ten to one I have lunch in the school canteen. Then it’s back to lessons. I leave school at a quarter past three and I get home at half past three. At home, I do my homework and watch TV. At six o’clock I have dinner. I go to bed at half past ten.

utterances.speaker: Mrs Magnus
utterances.text: Hi, Oscar, what would you like for lunch today?

utterances.speaker: Oscar
utterances.text: I’d like a lunch box, please.

utterances.speaker: Mrs Magnus
utterances.text: OK. Would you like a chicken sandwich or a cheese sandwich?

utterances.speaker: Oscar
utterances.text: A chicken sandwich, please.

utterances.speaker: Mrs Magnus
utterances.text: What dessert would you like?

utterances.speaker: Oscar
utterances.text: Umm, a biscuit, please.

utterances.speaker: Mrs Magnus
utterances.text: Oh, I’m sorry, Oscar. I haven’t got any biscuits left.

utterances.speaker: Oscar
utterances.text: That’s OK. A piece of cake, please.

utterances.speaker: Mrs Magnus
utterances.text: And what fruit would you like?

utterances.speaker: Oscar
utterances.text: Have you got oranges?

utterances.speaker: Mrs Magnus
utterances.text: Yes, we have.

utterances.speaker: Oscar
utterances.text: An orange, please.

utterances.speaker: Mrs Magnus
utterances.text: And to drink?

utterances.speaker: Oscar
utterances.text: An apple juice.

utterances.speaker: Mrs Magnus
utterances.text: Sorry, Oscar. We’ve got orange juice or water.

utterances.speaker: Oscar
utterances.text: OK. Then I’d like an orange juice, please.

utterances.speaker: Mrs Magnus
utterances.text: OK, there you go, Oscar. Enjoy.

utterances.speaker: Oscar
utterances.text: Thanks, Mrs Magnus.

utterances.speaker: Sally
utterances.text: Ben! Why don’t you have a rest and stop playing for a while? I’ve got homework. Ben!

utterances.speaker: Ben
utterances.text: What’s up, Sally?

utterances.speaker: Sally
utterances.text: I’ve got English and Geography homework. And you’re playing the guitar – badly!

utterances.speaker: Ben
utterances.text: Well, it’s my hobby and I have a good time when I practise. I love it.

utterances.speaker: Sally
utterances.text: Sure. But right now?

utterances.speaker: Ben
utterances.text: Well, yes! I’m practising now, then I can do my homework later.

utterances.speaker: Sally
utterances.text: Well, can you do your homework now, please? The same time as me? And then practise the guitar later?

utterances.speaker: Ben
utterances.text: Erm … well, yes, why not? But help me with my Maths homework, OK?

utterances.speaker: Sally
utterances.text: Oh, all right!

utterances.speaker: Jade
utterances.text: Mum, can I take judo lessons?

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Judo? Really? What for?

utterances.speaker: Jade
utterances.text: Well … it’s good exercise, and some of my friends are learning judo, too.

utterances.speaker: Dad
utterances.text: I think it’s a great idea.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Really? Judo for girls?

utterances.speaker: Jade
utterances.text: Mum!!

utterances.speaker: Dad
utterances.text: Yes, a friend of mine at work does judo. She loves it and she says it’s very good for making her strong and keeping her healthy.

utterances.speaker: Jade
utterances.text: That’s right, Dad. And maybe I can make some new friends, too.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Oh. Well. OK.

utterances.speaker: Jade
utterances.text: Thanks, Mum! Thanks, Dad!

utterances.speaker: Dad
utterances.text: Jade! I think that’s kung fu, not judo!

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Harry! It’s time for dinner.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Come on, Harry. Dinner’s ready.

utterances.speaker: Harry
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mum. I’m finishing something.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Harry, it’s dinnertime. Come and eat, we’re having dinner!

utterances.speaker: Harry
utterances.text: OK, Mum.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: You’re always on your phone. Playing games.

utterances.speaker: Harry
utterances.text: No, not games, Mum. Puzzles. I’m doing a crossword.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: A crossword? Oh, I hate crosswords. They’re too difficult.

utterances.speaker: Harry
utterances.text: I love them. They’re great exercise for my brain.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Are they? Well, OK. You know, you have to look after your brain, right?

utterances.speaker: Harry
utterances.text: That’s right. Just like you look after me, Mum.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Hello. Can I help you?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Hi. Yes, where can I find toothbrushes?

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: They’re just there on your right.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Oh yes. I didn’t see them. OK, I’ll take this one.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Is that all?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: No, there’s this toothpaste, too.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: OK. So that’s £4.30.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Here you are.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: And that’s 70p change. Have a nice day.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Are you all right there?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Yes, thanks. I just want a cover for my new phone. Have you got this one in red?

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Sorry, only black.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: OK, black’s fine. I’ll take it.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Right. That’s twelve ninety-nine please.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Can I pay with my contactless card?

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Of course. Just place it over here.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Great. That’s gone through. Would you like your receipt?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: No, it’s OK.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Do you need any help?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Hi. These trousers – can I try them on, please?

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Sure. What size do you take?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Not sure. 28 or 30.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: And do you want them in red? We’ve got other colours, too.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them but it’s the red ones I’m interested in.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: No problem. So why don’t you try both sizes? The changing rooms are in the corner.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Thanks!

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Can I help you?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Yeah. These football socks. How much are they? I can’t find the price.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Just a moment. They’re eight ninety-nine.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Fine. I’ll take them.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: OK, is that cash or card?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Cash.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: That’s great and here’s your change and receipt.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Thanks.
Now, look at the instructions for Part One. For each question, choose the correct answer. Look at question one. One. What are the girls talking about?

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Hey, Jo, I really like your new shoes.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: They’re not shoes. Look.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Oh, they’re boots. They look great.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Thanks. Now listen again. Two. When does Oliver play tennis?

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Hi, Oliver. Where are you going?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: To play tennis with Paula.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Tennis?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Yes, we always play twice a week. Now listen again. Three. Where is Brian?

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Have you got Fast Car magazine?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Yes, here you are.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: And can I have that newspaper for my dad?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: OK. That’s five pounds exactly. Now listen again. Four. What is Molly’s hobby?

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: That’s a nice camera, Molly.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Do you use it a lot?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Yes, I take a lot of photos to put on my blog.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: That’s interesting. Now listen again. Five. How much is the red jumper?

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: How much is that jumper?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: This one? It’s fourteen pounds, ninety-nine.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: No, sorry. I mean the red one.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Oh. Let me see. It’s seventeen pounds, ninety-nine. Oh, no, it’s not. It’s on sale. It’s only seven pounds, ninety-nine.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Great. I’ll take it. Now listen again.

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: So you’ve eaten here before?

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: Yes, it’s simple, but the food’s great. It’s perfect for a quick lunch.

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: What do they do?

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: The rolls are great. You can choose two fillings from tomato, tuna, cheese, curried chicken and sweet corn. Or you can have more fillings if you want to pay extra.

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: And if I don’t want a roll?

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: The soups are good. Chicken and mushroom, potato and onion and a spicy red pepper one – it’s really hot but it’s delicious.

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: That sounds good.

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: And we can’t leave without having a cake. They’ve got some great cakes. Carrot, chocolate or a coffee and walnut one that’s amazing!

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: And what about drinks?

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: The usual: orange juice, apple juice, tea, coffee or hot chocolate. Student’s Book Audioscript T123

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: Wow! You really do know this place well. How can you remember all that?

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: Easy. It’s all on the menu up there, on the wall behind you!

utterances.speaker: Assistant
utterances.text: Hello. Can I help you?

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: Yes, I’d like a cheese and tomato roll, please.

utterances.speaker: Assistant
utterances.text: Do you want the roll hot?

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: Assistant
utterances.text: Would you like something to drink?

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: Yes, I’d like an apple juice, please.

utterances.speaker: Assistant
utterances.text: So that’s a roll and an apple juice. Is that all?

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: Er, I’d like some carrot cake, too.

utterances.speaker: Assistant
utterances.text: OK, that’s £8 altogether.

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: Here you are.

utterances.speaker: Assistant
utterances.text: And that’s £2 change. The roll will be a few minutes. We’ll bring it to your table.

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Assistant
utterances.text: Enjoy your meal. And what can I get for you?

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: I’d like the chicken and mushroom soup, please, and an apple juice.

utterances.speaker: Assistant
utterances.text: OK. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: No, I think that’s all.

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: What! No cake? But you said …

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: I’m trying to be good. I only buy cake at the weekends.

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: Really?

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: Yes, I’m being careful with what I eat. Have you got a problem with that?

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: Assistant
utterances.text: OK, that’s £6.50.

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: Can I pay by card?

utterances.speaker: Assistant
utterances.text: Of course. Just put it in here.

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: It’s done.

utterances.speaker: Assistant
utterances.text: Thanks. We’ll bring the soup over in a minute or two.

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: Could you bring me a fork with it, too?

utterances.speaker: Assistant
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: A fork? What do you need a fork for? You can’t eat soup with a fork.

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: I’ve got my reasons. Don’t you worry about it.

utterances.speaker: Narrator
utterances.text: Moments later …

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: Well, you’re right. This is a good roll. How’s the soup?

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: Delicious. Would you like to try some?

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: No, I’m OK. My cake looks fantastic, doesn’t it?

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: Yes, it does. Mmmmm … it tastes fantastic, too!

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: Hey, what are you doing?

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: Mmmmm. That is a good cake!

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: But you said, cake only at the weekends.

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: I said I only buy cake at the weekends.

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: And?

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: Well, you bought this cake. I’ve got no problem eating your cake.

utterances.speaker: Steve
utterances.text: And that explains the fork.

utterances.speaker: Hannah
utterances.text: Yes, it does. Now hurry up and finish your roll before I eat all your cake.

utterances.text: Good morning. Can I help you?

utterances.speaker: Customer
utterances.text: I’d like some coffee, please.

utterances.speaker: Assistant
utterances.text: Do you want milk or sugar?

utterances.speaker: Customer

utterances.speaker: Assistant
utterances.text: Would you like something to eat?

utterances.speaker: Assistant

Dialogue 1

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: What are you doing, Lori?

utterances.speaker: Lori
utterances.text: I’m looking for my T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: Your T-shirt? You’ve got lots! Which one are you looking for?

utterances.speaker: Lori
utterances.text: The red one with the flower on it. I can’t find it anywhere and I’ve got to go out in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: Where are you going?

utterances.speaker: Lori
utterances.text: To the cinema with Lucy and Darcy. I want to look nice. Oh, I can’t find it!

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: Do you want to borrow one of mine?

utterances.speaker: Lori
utterances.text: Can I? Thanks, Olivia, you’re the best.

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: Sure. Just get one from my room but don’t make a mess.

utterances.speaker: Lori
utterances.text: Don’t worry. No mess, I promise. Can I borrow your red boots, too?

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: You mean my new ones? No, you can’t.

utterances.speaker: Lori
utterances.text: Oh no, really? Why not? They’re really cool!

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: I know I am the world’s best sister, Lori, but there are some times when I have to say ‘no’! Dialogue 2

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: Mum? Have we got any plans this weekend?

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: I don’t think so. Why?

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: There’s a party at Nathan’s place. Can I go?

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Well, that depends … When is it?

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: Saturday night. 8 o’clock.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Sure. That’s fine. Where does Nathan live?

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: He’s out in Foxton. His family have got an amazing house.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Foxton? That’s five kilometres from here. And I guess there are no buses at that time of night.

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: Umm, no, I don’t think so. Well, no actually, there aren’t any buses, no.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Right. So come on. Let’s hear the next question, Tom.

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: Any chance of a lift, Mum?

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Of course, but I need to pick you up by midnight at the latest. I need my sleep, you know.

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: No problem, Mum. Thanks so much!
Now look at Part Three. For each question, choose the correct answer. Look at the questions now. You have twenty seconds. Listen to Jackie talking to Oliver about his family.

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: Hi, Oliver. Was the party good?

utterances.speaker: Oliver
utterances.text: Party?

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: Yes, your uncle’s birthday party. Remember? Last Friday evening?

utterances.speaker: Oliver
utterances.text: Last Friday, of course. Yes, it was great.

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: Have you got any photos?

utterances.speaker: Oliver
utterances.text: Yes, I took some on my phone. Do you want to have a look?

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: Of course I do.

utterances.speaker: Oliver
utterances.text: OK, so this is my Uncle Dan. It was his birthday.

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: I know. How old is he?

utterances.speaker: Oliver
utterances.text: Let’s think. He’s twenty years older than me. I’m fourteen so …

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: So he’s thirty-four.

utterances.speaker: Oliver
utterances.text: That’s right. Anyway, so that’s my Uncle Dan and this is his wife, Anna.

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: She’s very pretty.

utterances.speaker: Oliver
utterances.text: And that’s their son, Mike. He’s only four. He’s really funny.

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: Ahhh. He’s so cute. So who’s that girl next to you in this photo?

utterances.speaker: Oliver
utterances.text: That’s my sister!

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: What? Carla?

utterances.speaker: Oliver
utterances.text: No, my other sister, Ruth.

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: Your little sister, Ruth? No way.

utterances.speaker: Oliver
utterances.text: Yes, she’s ten now. Now listen again.

utterances.speaker: DJ
utterances.text: So today we have a question for listeners, and it is: what’s your favourite room, and why? Our first caller is … hello. What’s your name?

utterances.speaker: Jo
utterances.text: Hi there! My name’s Jo.

utterances.speaker: DJ
utterances.text: OK Jo, so tell us, what’s your favourite room?

utterances.speaker: Jo
utterances.text: It’s my grandfather’s playroom.

utterances.speaker: DJ
utterances.text: Your grandfather’s got a playroom? Really?

utterances.speaker: Jo
utterances.text: Yeah. It’s the room with his model trains. My grandad still lives in the house he lived in when he was a boy. And he has a little room with his trains. I love looking at his trains.

utterances.speaker: DJ
utterances.text: OK. And why is it special for you?

utterances.speaker: Jo
utterances.text: Because he’s so happy there, and we sit and talk, and I feel very relaxed. It’s lovely.

utterances.speaker: DJ
utterances.text: It sounds great, Jo. Thank you. Now who’s next? What’s your name and what’s your favourite room?

utterances.speaker: Andrew
utterances.text: Hi. I’m Andrew and my favourite room is the music room at my school.

utterances.speaker: DJ
utterances.text: OK, Andrew. And why’s that?

utterances.speaker: Andrew
utterances.text: It’s because I love playing the drums, but I can’t have drums at home, so I go into the music room at school and practise there. After school. No one cares. I have a lot of fun!

utterances.speaker: DJ
utterances.text: Sounds good to me! Thanks, Andrew. Next caller please! Hello!

utterances.speaker: Paula
utterances.text: Hello, I’m Paula. My favourite room is our kitchen at home. I love it there because that’s where all of us sit and have our breakfast and dinner, and we’re a family together. It makes me feel really nice and warm.

utterances.speaker: DJ
utterances.text: Nice and warm. That’s a good reason.

utterances.speaker: Paula
utterances.text: Yeah, and kind of … I don’t know, safe.

utterances.speaker: DJ
utterances.text: Excellent, Paula, thank you. And now we have … hello?

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: Hi. Tom here. I don’t know if it’s really my favourite room, but the best room in my whole life was in a hotel.

utterances.speaker: DJ
utterances.text: Oh right. That’s interesting! Tell us more!

utterances.speaker: Tom
utterances.text: We all went to Brazil last year, and we got to the hotel in Rio de Janeiro very early in the morning and it was still quite dark. But then the day started and I opened the window to see Copacabana beach. Brilliant! I loved that room. We were there for five days and …

utterances.speaker: DJ
utterances.text: Thanks, Tom. I’m sorry, there’s no more time. OK, now let’s … .

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Hi, Jack. How was school?

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Oh, fine. Mum, can I bring some friends round tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Sure. Who?

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Oh, probably Rachel and Steve, maybe Leo.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: OK. Not Markus?

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Er, no.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Oh? Why not?

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Well, we’re not really friends any more.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Seriously? I thought you two were best friends.

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Yeah, we were. But you know, we had an argument – he said something I didn’t like – so he’s not my friend any more.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: And what did he say?

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Well, he called me silly. Friends don’t do that.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Jack, do you remember Mrs Gordon? Janice? She’s a friend of mine.

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. She was your friend at school too, wasn’t she?

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Yes, and we’re still friends now, 20 years later. Her mother was a friend of my mother’s. Anyway, one day at school, well, we had an argument and I said something really horrible to her.

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: It doesn’t matter. But she walked away and said, ‘I never want to see you again.’ I was really upset about that and I shouted, ‘Same here!’ or something. Then the next day, at school, she came up to me with a big smile and said, ‘Hi, Jenny, you OK?’

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Really?

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Yes, I was completely surprised and I asked her, I said, ‘Aren’t you angry with me?’ And she said something I still remember. She said: ‘Well, yes, I was angry but last night I thought of all the nice things you always say to me and the nice things you do. I want to think about that, not something you said because you were angry.’ And those words of hers, well, they almost made me cry. And here we are, twenty years later, still friends.

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Wow. Cool story, Mum.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: So I think it’s a real shame that after such a long time, you can’t still be friends with Markus.

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: You’re right. Wow, so many times he helped me with my homework, listened to me when I had a problem.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: That’s right. So he called you silly one time? So what? And you know, sometimes you are stupid – just like everyone else.

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Yes. Mum, I’m going out. Round to Markus’ place, OK?

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Good idea, Jack, and why don’t you take him a present to say sorry?

Now look at Part Five. For each question, choose the correct answer. Look at questions 1 – 5 now. You have 15 seconds. You will hear Jen talking to Mark about her room. Which piece of furniture did each person give Jen? Student’s Book Audioscript T125

utterances.speaker: Mark
utterances.text: Wow, Jen – I love your bedroom. It’s so cool. Where did you get that armchair?

utterances.speaker: Jen
utterances.text: My grandpa gave it to me. He didn’t want it any more.

utterances.speaker: Mark
utterances.text: Did he give you the sofa, too?

utterances.speaker: Jen
utterances.text: No, that was a birthday present from Dad.

utterances.speaker: Mark
utterances.text: You’re so lucky. My room’s just big enough for a bed!

utterances.speaker: Jen
utterances.text: I know but you’re lucky because you’ve got brothers and a sister.

utterances.speaker: Mark
utterances.text: Lucky? I’m not so sure! These curtains are great. They make the room really warm. Were they a present?

utterances.speaker: Jen
utterances.text: Yes, Mum got them for me but I chose them. My Aunt Abi bought me the carpet from the same shop.

utterances.speaker: Mark
utterances.text: And you’ve got your own desk, too!

utterances.speaker: Jen
utterances.text: Yes, I got that from my Uncle Tim. Oh, no, that’s wrong, I didn’t. I got it from my other uncle, Uncle Simon. It’s really old but I like it. Did you see my lamp?

utterances.speaker: Mark
utterances.text: Yes, it’s the best thing in your room.

utterances.speaker: Jen
utterances.text: That’s because you gave it to me! Now listen again.

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: … and some people think that only older people – like me – can be inventors. But they’re wrong, you know? Here’s one example – a young man in South Africa, only 17 years old, saw a problem with water quality and he invented a gel that people can use to wash, to have a bath, even if there is no water. He was only 17! So, you guys out there, you shouldn’t wait. Just go ahead and do it, OK? So now, we don’t have much time, any questions? Boy 1  Did the boy in South Africa get rich?

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: I really don’t know. I hope so! But that’s not the point. He invented something that made other people’s lives better. He didn’t think: how can I get rich? He thought: how can I help people? And that’s the place you should start. You should start with an idea to help other people. To make lives easier and, hopefully, better.

utterances.speaker: Girl
utterances.text: I’ve got lots of ideas for inventions.

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: Oh? Like what?

utterances.speaker: Girl
utterances.text: Well, I don’t want to say.

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: Good for you! Be very careful. You should only talk to people that you trust, OK? But another thing: you say you’ve got lots of ideas, and that’s great. But don’t try to work on all of them at the same time. You should say to yourself: which idea is the best one? And then you should try to work more on that idea.

utterances.speaker: Girl
utterances.text: And should I forget the other ones?

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: No, no, no! Absolutely not. I mean, I’m sure you won’t forget them anyway. Yes, another question? Boy 2  Is being an inventor a job? I mean, should I leave school and just start inventing things?

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: Hahaha, it sounds like a good idea, right? But to start, when you leave school, I think you should get a job and invent things as a hobby. Boy 2  Why?

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: Well, you have to live, don’t you? And maybe your first invention isn’t successful, so where is the money for you to live? No, you should make sure that you’ve got a job and then see if the inventions work out. And, look, I’m afraid we’re out of time, we have to stop now. I hope the talk was interesting for you all. Good luck and goodbye!

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: Gemma, how do you feel about sport?

utterances.speaker: Gemma
utterances.text: I’m not interested in sport. I really don’t like it. I mean, I like exercise so I go for walks and I like swimming, oh I run a lot too, that’s great – but I just don’t like sport, you know, the idea where you try to win, to beat other people. And I hate sport on TV – I leave the room! And I don’t go to sports events like football matches – why do people pay so much money to watch 22 men run after a ball?

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: Andy, how do you feel about sport?

utterances.speaker: Andy
utterances.text: Well, I like running a lot. At school I play football but that’s because I have to, all the boys play football, and it’s OK, I mean I don’t hate it, but I don’t really like team games and sports very much. I like doing things alone and I think that’s why I love running, it’s just me and not other people. I’m not a very good runner but I just love trying to run a little faster than the last time, do you know what I mean?

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: Tracey, how do you feel about sport?

utterances.speaker: Tracey
utterances.text: Well, I absolutely love skateboarding, of course! It’s just the best thing in the world. Some of my family say it isn’t really a sport but they don’t know anything. I spend hours practising moves. There’s a skate-park with a really good ramp, it’s not far from where I live. I’m there all the time. It’s the only sport I like really. I mean, I kind of like football but really that’s only because some of my friends are into it. But skateboarding, that’s my thing.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: Paul, how do you feel about sport?

utterances.speaker: Paul
utterances.text: When I was a kid I didn’t like any sports at all. I thought: ‘I’m just not good at things like running and jumping’ but about a year ago I saw some gymnastics on TV and now I love it. There’s a sports centre in my town where I can do gymnastics. I can’t do it at school because they haven’t got anywhere, but I go to the sports centre every weekend and some evenings too, to do as much gymnastics as I can.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: Ryan, how do you feel about sport?

utterances.speaker: Ryan
utterances.text: Sport? Wonderful! I’m a real sports fanatic. I mean, I think about sport all the time. I watch almost everything on TV – football, tennis, swimming, everything. And I do a lot of sport too – my favourite’s football, of course, and I’m really not bad at football. I’m in the school team too. And I’m also learning to ski. My family went to Italy last year. We went skiing – it was fantastic and I want to do more.
Now look at Part Four. For each question, choose the correct answer. You will hear a man talking to his son. What does the man want his son to do?

utterances.speaker: Father
utterances.text: You’re still doing your homework, Mike?

utterances.speaker: Son
utterances.text: Yeah, it’s a lot.

utterances.speaker: Father
utterances.text: Hmm. I was hoping we could go for a bike ride. I’ve got an idea. I’ll help you a bit, then we can go sooner, OK?

utterances.speaker: Son
utterances.text: Sounds great, Dad. Now listen again. You will hear a girl, Kate, talking about shopping. Why did she buy the camera?

utterances.speaker: Kate
utterances.text: Hey, have a look at my new camera. I wanted it for a long time, and then this new shop in Market Street opened yesterday. And guess what – they had a special offer. I wanted it in pink, but they only had it in blue. But that’s not a problem. Now listen again. You will hear a woman talking to her daughter. What’s the weather like?

utterances.speaker: Nancy
utterances.text: Ready, Mum.

utterances.speaker: Mum
utterances.text: Oh, thanks so much, Nancy. Here’s the money. And don’t forget to take your coat. It’s raining. I don’t want you to catch a cold. Now listen again. You will hear a teacher talking to her student, Sebastian. What is he going to do after school?

utterances.speaker: Miss Miller
utterances.text: Sebastian, I’m sorry to hear your mum’s in hospital.

utterances.speaker: Sebastian
utterances.text: Thanks, Miss Miller.

utterances.speaker: Miss Miller
utterances.text: Please say hello from me when you see her next.

utterances.speaker: Sebastian
utterances.text: I will. I’m catching the bus so I can see her there after my final lesson.

utterances.speaker: Miss Miller
utterances.text: Look, you don’t have to do your homework today. Better stay with her for a bit longer. She’ll like that.

utterances.speaker: Sebastian
utterances.text: OK. Now listen again. You will hear two friends talking about their day. What did they do?

utterances.speaker: Boy A
utterances.text: It’s been a great day.

utterances.speaker: Boy B
utterances.text: That’s true. The adventure park was fun. I loved it.

utterances.speaker: Boy A
utterances.text: Me too. But I’m really tired now.

utterances.speaker: Boy B
utterances.text: Well, it’s good we didn’t come on our bikes. You can rest on the bus home. Now listen again.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: You know so much about the wildlife here, PK. How come?

utterances.speaker: PK
utterances.text: My family are San, bush people, and I learned about nature from the time when I was a child. I was born in the Kalahari.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: And you grew up and found your wife here?

utterances.speaker: PK
utterances.text: Yes, finding a wife here was very interesting.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: Tell us more.

utterances.speaker: PK
utterances.text: Yes, let’s say a young man wants to marry a girl. So he has to ask her father and he says before you can marry my daughter, you have to do a task.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: OK. So what type of task does the young man have to do, PK?

utterances.speaker: PK
utterances.text: Well, for example, he has to show that he can take a kill away from a lion.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: What do you mean ‘take a kill away from a lion’?

utterances.speaker: PK
utterances.text: Well, imagine a lion kills an antelope or another large animal. The young man has to find that lion and get the meat, so he can show that he has courage. That’s important for his future family.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: Wow, but how can you do that? How can you find a lion and its kill?

utterances.speaker: PK
utterances.text: You have to look. You have to look for the big birds, the vultures. They are watching the lion because they want some of the meat.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: OK, so let’s say you find the lion and its kill. How can you then get the meat? Isn’t that dangerous?

utterances.speaker: PK
utterances.text: Yes, of course the lion is dangerous. You mustn’t take the meat away from the lion at night. You have to do that during the day.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: Why’s that?

utterances.speaker: PK
utterances.text: During the day it’s very hot. And the big cats can’t run fast when it’s hot. A man can run even when it’s very hot, but lions can’t.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: PK
utterances.text: No, they can’t. When they eat some meat, they feel very, very hot and get very tired. So they often just lie around and they sleep all the time during the day. At night they are more dangerous because they don’t sleep. And at night their eyes are better than your eyes. So you can’t get the kill from the lion at night.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: OK, so you have to do that during the day. But what do you do to get the kill from the lion?

utterances.speaker: PK
utterances.text: OK. So let’s say the lion is sleeping. You hold your spear in your hand. You have to be very quiet. And you go up to that lion.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: Do you attack him with your spear? Kill him?

utterances.speaker: PK
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. You just go up to him and shout, ‘Arrrrggggghhhhh!’ You mustn’t hurt him or kill him, just surprise him, shock him, so he runs away.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: Wow!

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: Hey Connor. What are you doing this weekend?

utterances.speaker: Connor
utterances.text: Hi! I’m quite busy actually. Why?

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: Well, it’s just that we’ve got that History test coming up. Do you want to study together?

utterances.speaker: Connor
utterances.text: That would be great! But, let me see. Saturday morning is no good. I’m playing football. It’s the cup final and I can’t miss that.

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: Of course not. OK, so what about Friday night?

utterances.speaker: Connor
utterances.text: Hmmm, I’m sorry. I can’t. I’m busy. Dad’s taking me to the sports centre to watch the basketball game, but it doesn’t finish until 10 pm.

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: Yeah, that’s a bit late. OK, how about Saturday afternoon. Any chance?

utterances.speaker: Connor
utterances.text: Mmm. Saturday afternoon, Saturday afternoon. It’s my brother’s birthday, so we’re going to the restaurant to celebrate. You know, that new American diner on the high street.

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: Oh, yeah, I’ve heard it’s very good. What time do you think you’ll finish there?

utterances.speaker: Connor
utterances.text: Probably about 5 pm, but then I’m meeting Nathan. We’re going to see the new Spider-Man film at the cinema. Hey, would you like to come?

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: Hmmm, Spider-Man – not really my thing. So thanks but no thanks. I guess that just leaves Sunday.

utterances.speaker: Connor
utterances.text: Yeah, Sunday. Hmmmm, that’s a problem, too.

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: Connor
utterances.text: Well, my grandparents are coming over and we’re taking them to that outdoor museum.

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: Oh, the one with all the cool old buildings?

utterances.speaker: Connor
utterances.text: That’s right. My grandad loves that sort of stuff. I’d invite you, but I’m really sorry, we haven’t got any room in the car. Student’s Book Audioscript T127

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: I don’t want to see old buildings, Connor. I want to study for the test.

utterances.speaker: Connor
utterances.text: Yeah, of course. Sunday evening maybe, but only after 8 pm. I’ve got a piano lesson from 7 to 8 and we won’t be back from the museum much before 6 pm.

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: No, that’s too late.

utterances.speaker: Connor
utterances.text: What about next weekend? I’ve got loads of free time next weekend.

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: I’d love to! But there’s a problem.

utterances.speaker: Connor
utterances.text: What’s that?

utterances.speaker: Olivia
utterances.text: The test is on Monday. This Monday. First thing in the morning!

Now look at Part Two. For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Look at questions 1 – 5 now. You have ten seconds. Hello and welcome to the Blue Water Shopping Centre. We are the largest shopping centre in the North East and have more than 300 shops on four different floors as well as 14 restaurants and a cinema – all found on the 5th floor. The shopping centre is easy to reach by road, just follow the signs from Hull city centre. There’s a car park for 5,000 cars. And for each hour that you park there it only costs £2. There is also a regular free bus service between the mall and Hull city centre. Buses leave every 15 minutes. The shopping mall opens at 9 am. All shops close at 7.30 pm during the week and on Sundays, and at 9 pm on Saturdays. The restaurants and cinema stay open until 11 pm. Thank you for listening. If you wish to hear this message again, press one. If you want to talk to someone, please stay on the line. For more information, visit us online at www.bwshopping.com. Now listen again.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Are you OK?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: No, ouch. My knee! Aaargh!

utterances.speaker: Girl
utterances.text: I ate a lot of food last night. My stomach really isn’t too good this morning.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Don’t eat so quickly – you’ll bite your tongue.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Ouch!

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: See? I told you!

utterances.speaker: Dad
utterances.text: Are you all right, Lydia?

utterances.speaker: Lydia
utterances.text: No, I’m not, Dad. I’m not well at all.

utterances.speaker: Dad
utterances.text: What’s the matter with you?

utterances.speaker: Lydia
utterances.text: I’ve got a really bad stomach ache.

utterances.speaker: Dad
utterances.text: Do you think it was something you ate?

utterances.speaker: Liam
utterances.text: No, not just one thing. She ate loads.

utterances.speaker: Dad
utterances.text: Don’t be mean, Liam. Your sister doesn’t feel great.

utterances.speaker: Lydia
utterances.text: He’s right, Dad. I think I was too hungry. I didn’t have any lunch at school today.

utterances.speaker: Dad
utterances.text: I think you need to just go and lie down for a while. I’m sure you’ll feel better soon.

utterances.speaker: Lydia
utterances.text: OK, Dad. I will. I’ll just try and rest.

utterances.speaker: Dad
utterances.text: And don’t worry about the washing- up. I’m sure your brother will do that.

utterances.speaker: Liam
utterances.text: What? Me??!!

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Come in, Tim. Take a seat.

utterances.speaker: Tim
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: So how can I help you today?

utterances.speaker: Tim
utterances.text: It’s my elbow. It’s really painful. Look.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Hmm, yes, it does look a bit bruised. So what happened?

utterances.speaker: Tim
utterances.text: Well, it’s a bit of a silly story really. I got home from school yesterday and I didn’t have my key with me. I left it in my locker at school so I tried to open the door with my elbow.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Oh, I see. And it didn’t open?

utterances.speaker: Tim
utterances.text: No, it didn’t.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Well, I don’t think it’s anything too serious. You need to put some ice on it, and take some painkillers if it hurts too much.

utterances.speaker: Tim
utterances.text: So, it’s not broken?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: No, it isn’t. You’re able to move it so I’m not too worried. But next time you forget your key, just wait for your parents to get home.

utterances.speaker: Tim
utterances.text: OK, Doctor. I will.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Hello, John. What can I do for you?

utterances.speaker: John
utterances.text: It’s my neck.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: OK. And what’s the problem with it? Does it hurt?

utterances.speaker: John
utterances.text: Yes, it does. I can hardly move it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Oh dear. What happened?

utterances.speaker: John
utterances.text: I’m not sure. I went to bed last night and when I woke up it was really hurting.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Did you do any sport yesterday?

utterances.speaker: John
utterances.text: No, I didn’t. But I did sleep with the window open. My grandmother thinks the cold air made it hurt but I’m not so sure.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: No, I don’t think there’s any connection there. OK, well, let’s have a look at it. Can you take your shirt off for me, please?

utterances.speaker: John
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Mr Gardner
utterances.text: Hello?

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: Oh hi, Mr Gardner. It’s Jackie here, Jackie Martin, Andy’s friend from school.

utterances.speaker: Mr Gardner
utterances.text: Yes, Jackie. Hi. Listen. I’m afraid Andy’s not here. He’ll be back in about an hour, I think.

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: Oh dear. I really need to talk to him.

utterances.speaker: Mr Gardner
utterances.text: Do you want to leave a message?

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: Yes please. Um. Well, the thing is, I’ve got a problem with my homework. The Science homework.

utterances.speaker: Mr Gardner
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: And I need to finish it tonight because we’re going away tomorrow, for the weekend.

utterances.speaker: Mr Gardner
utterances.text: Right. So, you want Andy to call you tonight?

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: Yes please. As soon as he gets back.

utterances.speaker: Mr Gardner
utterances.text: ‘As soon as you get back!’ OK. Has he got your number?

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: I’m not sure. I’ve got a new mobile, so can I tell you?

utterances.speaker: Mr Gardner
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Mr Gardner
utterances.text: 213 223. OK, got that, Jackie. Leave it to me. I’ll make sure he gets the message.

utterances.speaker: Jackie
utterances.text: Thanks, Mr Gardner. Thanks very much. Bye.

utterances.speaker: Mr Gardner
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: Hello again. Right. He’s visited more than a hundred countries. He’s taken thousands of photos and published them in travel magazines. He’s got a very popular travel blog. But he’s taken a break today to talk about how to travel well. Richard Ward, thank you for coming today.

utterances.speaker: Richard
utterances.text: Thanks for inviting me.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: So you’ve just completed your tenth year of travelling.

utterances.speaker: Richard
utterances.text: That’s right. Ten years without spending more than a week back home. Well, my parents’ home. I’ve never had my own home.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: And to celebrate your ten years, you’ve made a list of top things to do when you travel.

utterances.speaker: Richard
utterances.text: That’s right. And I’m hoping to publish them in a book later this year.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: Have you ever written a book before?

utterances.speaker: Richard
utterances.text: No, I haven’t. This will be my first.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: How exciting. Now, on your website, there are twenty tips for travelling. We can’t talk about all of them so can I ask you, what’s your number one tip?

utterances.speaker: Richard
utterances.text: Well, that’s difficult. My number one? Hmm. OK. I’m going to say: ‘Get off the beaten track’. I mean, try and go to places that other people don’t go to. Of course, it’s great to see all those famous places that everyone wants to see. But if you explore a bit further, go to other places, you’ll discover much more interesting things, you know? On my blog I talk about an important difference: the difference between travellers and tourists. A tourist always stays on the beaten track. A traveller likes to leave it. Of course, you might get lost …

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: And have you ever got lost?

utterances.speaker: Richard
utterances.text: Oh yes, hundreds of times. In fact another of my tips is ‘try to get lost’! It’s part of the fun of travelling. If you get lost sometimes, you can find amazing things, great people.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: OK, let’s talk about things to take with you. Another tip you have is: ‘always take a scarf’. Why?

utterances.speaker: Richard
utterances.text: Well, a scarf is a really useful thing. You can wrap it around you to keep you warm or to keep the sun off. You can carry things in it, too, or tie things together.

utterances.speaker: Interviewer
utterances.text: Well, I want to talk some more, Richard. But first it’s time for some music and …

Now look at Part Five. For each question, choose the correct answer. Look at questions 1 – 5 now. You have 15 seconds. You will hear Jack talking to a friend about his transport project. How does each person get to school?

utterances.speaker: Leah
utterances.text: So have you done your transport project, Jack?

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Yes, I’ve got all the information and results.

utterances.speaker: Leah
utterances.text: So any surprises?

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Not really. Like me, most people walk to school.

utterances.speaker: Leah
utterances.text: Me too. What about Olivia? What does she do?

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Well, the most popular type of transport is taking the bus. I think 14 people take the bus, including Olivia.

utterances.speaker: Leah
utterances.text: What about Rashid? Doesn’t he come by bus?

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: No, he comes with his mum in her car.

utterances.speaker: Leah
utterances.text: So how many come by car?

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Eight.

utterances.speaker: Leah
utterances.text: And what about Morris?

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Well, he actually cycles to school. He likes the exercise.

utterances.speaker: Leah
utterances.text: I see. So what’s the most unusual type of transport? Does anyone go by scooter?

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: No scooter riders. And the unusual … ? Definitely, Leslie’s way – by boat.

utterances.speaker: Leah
utterances.text: Boat? Really?

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Yes, boat. She lives on the other side of the river so she takes it every morning.

utterances.speaker: Leah
utterances.text: Wow, that’s quite a journey.

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: It’s not the longest journey though.

utterances.speaker: Leah
utterances.text: Why? Who has the longest one?

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Adam. He has to take two trains to get to school.

utterances.speaker: Leah
utterances.text: That’s right. He lives with his mum, doesn’t he?

utterances.speaker: Jack
utterances.text: Yes, she moved town but he wanted to keep coming here. So it’s two trains and about an hour to get here. Now listen again.
